written.description: Judges an MCP server's tool definitions three ways, by YARA rule, by hosted inspection API and by asking a model, so a poisoned tool description has to clear more than one kind of reader.

alive.last_commit_message:
docs(behavioral): fix the programmatic usage examples (#320)

* docs(behavioral): fix the programmatic usage examples

The "Programmatic Usage" section of docs/behavioral-scanning.md did not
run. The snippets failed with:

- Scanner has no scan_source_code(); behavioral scanning is done with
  BehavioralCodeAnalyzer.analyze(), which returns SecurityFinding objects
  (one per MCP tool, severity "SAFE" when nothing was found), the same
  way docs/architecture.md and the CLI use it.
- the helpers live in mcpscanner.core.result, there is no
  mcpscanner.result module.
- format_results_by_analyzer() formats one scan result, so it has to be
  called per result instead of with the whole list. filter_results_by_severity()
  and format_results_as_json() take scan result objects, so the example now
  wraps the findings in ToolScanResult first.
- filter_results_by_severity(results, "medium") returns only MEDIUM
  findings, not "MEDIUM and above" as the comment claimed.

* docs(behavioral): keep failed and same-named tools visible in the examples

Review follow-up for the Programmatic Usage examples:

- Check that the path exists before scanning. analyze() treats any
  string that is not an existing file or directory as inline source, so
  a mistyped path used to come back as an empty, clean-looking result.
- Check analyzer.analysis_errors after the scan. analyze() counts read
  and parse failures there instead of raising.
- Say that an empty list means no MCP tool was found, not that the code
  is safe.
- Name each tool by details["source_file"] and the function name, so a
  directory scan does not merge two tools that share a function name.
- Wrap a finding whose analysis_status is "errored" (severity UNKNOWN)
  as a "failed" ToolScanResult with an analyzer error. It is then shown
  as incomplete instead of as a threat, and it stays in both the HIGH
  and the MEDIUM filtered lists instead of dropping out of both.
- The Limitations section no longer says the analyzer is Python only;
  it scans every language listed under Supported Languages.
